hero.headline: Border closure over screwworm outbreak disrupts cattle trade between Texas and Mexico
hero.body:
A flesh-eating parasite has returned to the United States for the first time in six decades, triggering emergency restrictions on livestock movement between Texas and Mexico. The new world screwworm fly was confirmed in a calf in south Texas, approximately 50 miles from the Mexican border, marking the first detection in the state since 1966.

The parasite's reappearance has created immediate international consequences. Canada has banned cattle imports from Texas, while a second infected calf was subsequently identified in the state. Texas Governor Greg Abbott declared a disaster over the outbreak as state and federal officials mobilized to contain the spread.

The screwworm fly poses a serious threat to livestock agriculture. Female flies lay eggs in open wounds on warm-blooded animals, and the larvae feed on blood and living flesh. If untreated, infected animals can die. The parasite was eradicated from the United States in the 1970s after causing tens of millions of dollars in losses. Officials are particularly concerned given that beef prices across the country are currently at record highs.

"For months, the screwworm has advanced rapidly through Mexico," said Sid Miller, Texas agriculture commissioner. "Even though billions of sterile flies have been dispersed by USDA, the screwworm has still advanced over 1,100 miles from southern Mexico to Texas."

The USDA has defended its response, with Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins stating there is no threat of mass infestation. She emphasized that the Texas case was the first confirmed detection since 1966 and that there is "no reason to believe this incursion will result in establishment of the pest in our country."

To combat the outbreak, the USDA announced in March that it had partnered with the Army Corps of Engineers and Mortenson Construction to build a new sterile fly production facility at Moore Airbase in Edinburg, Texas. The program relies on releasing sterile male flies, which mate with wild females and produce eggs that do not hatch, gradually reducing the population over time.

Miller has urged the Trump administration to deploy the screwworm adult suppression system, or Swass, which combines attractants, bait, and targeted insecticides to reduce adult populations before sterile fly releases complete the eradication effort. This approach successfully eliminated screwworms from Mexico and Texas during previous campaigns.

The parasite's southward progression through Mexico last year forced ranchers to resort to crude treatments. High medicine costs led some to apply gasoline or lime to open wounds in attempts to extract worms. The border restrictions now prevent Texas cattle from reaching those markets while disrupting the traditional livestock trade that has long connected the two countries' agricultural sectors.

cards.headline: US strikes Iranian radar sites after intercepting drones fired at Bahrain and Kuwait
cards.body:
US and Iran Exchange Fire in Latest Test of Fragile Ceasefire

The United States and Iran exchanged military strikes in the Gulf on Saturday, marking another serious challenge to the tenuous ceasefire between the two countries. Air raid sirens sounded in Bahrain and Kuwait as the confrontation unfolded, with both nations' militaries scrambling to intercept incoming threats.

The US military said it shot down four Iranian attack drones launched toward the Strait of Hormuz and responded by striking Iranian coastal surveillance radar sites on the islands of Sirik and Qeshm Island. US Central Command stated the drones "posed an immediate threat to regional maritime traffic," while the radar strikes were intended to "defend against further attacks."

Hours later, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps retaliated, firing seven ballistic missiles toward Kuwait and Bahrain. The US military said six missiles were intercepted and one failed to reach its target. "There are currently no reports of harm to US personnel," Central Command stated, adding that Iranian claims of damaging US 5th Fleet headquarters in Bahrain were false.

The IRGC said it had targeted enemy bases in the Gulf following the American strikes. Kuwait's military confirmed it was intercepting drones and missiles launched at the country, while Bahrain issued air raid alerts instructing residents to move to safe locations.

Kuwait's foreign ministry condemned the attacks as a "serious escalation" and "flagrant violation of its sovereignty," saying the country reserved the right to defend itself. The latest exchange represents the continuing pattern of tit-for-tat military incidents that have strained diplomatic efforts.

The confrontation comes as the Trump administration pressures both countries to reach a permanent agreement. US and Iranian negotiators have spent weeks trying to extend the ceasefire by 60 days and begin new talks on Iran's nuclear program, but neither side appears ready to compromise. An Iranian official said the negotiations have reached a deadlock.

Trump told reporters on Friday that the situation with Iran "seems to be going quite well," but acknowledged the difficulty of negotiations. "It's a very hard thing for Iran," he said, adding that Iran had things it never expected to have to do.

The instability has extended beyond the US-Iran conflict. Fighting in Lebanon, where Israeli forces have seized large areas of the south, also threatens efforts to end the broader regional war and reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Iran has demanded that any lasting ceasefire extend to Lebanon, creating additional complications in negotiations.

The repeated military exchanges have created wider economic consequences. The World Food Programme reported that millions of people were being pushed into hunger due to the conflict's effects on energy and food prices.

cards.headline: Ukrainian drones strike St Petersburg in attack Russia calls unprecedented
cards.teaser: Russia described a Ukrainian drone attack on St Petersburg as unprecedented, prompting the city's governor to urge residents to stay indoors for the first time since the war began.
cards.body:
Ukrainian drones targeted St Petersburg, Russia's second-largest city, in an attack that Russian officials described as unprecedented. The strike prompted the city's governor to issue an unprecedented directive urging residents to remain indoors—the first such guidance since the war began.

President Vladimir Putin responded by announcing plans to strengthen Russia's air defenses against Ukrainian drone attacks. The assault reached deep into Russian territory and disrupted Putin's economic forum taking place in his hometown, underscoring the expanding reach of Ukrainian long-range drone capabilities.

cards.headline: Chip sector loses $1.3 trillion in market value in single-day selloff
cards.teaser: Semiconductor stocks suffered their worst trading day in six years as AI trade momentum reversed.
cards.body:
A sharp selloff in artificial intelligence chip stocks triggered a broad market decline on Friday. The Nasdaq fell 4 percent in its largest single-day drop in over a year, while the S&P 500 and Dow Jones also declined by 2.6 percent and 1.3 percent respectively.

The selloff occurred despite positive employment data showing US employers added 172,000 jobs in May, keeping the unemployment rate steady at 4.3 percent. The labor market resilience stood in contrast to the stock market's sharp reversal, as investors reassessed valuations in the semiconductor sector.

cards.headline: U.S. crude oil inventories fall to lowest level since 2004
cards.body:
America's crude oil stockpiles have dropped to their lowest level in more than two decades, marking the sixth consecutive week of declines. The shrinking reserves come as the Trump administration's conflict with Iran disrupts global oil markets and pushes exports from the Gulf Coast to record levels.

The Strategic Petroleum Reserve and commercial crude inventories have both declined sharply in recent weeks. Record exports from Gulf Coast refineries have accelerated the drawdown, as American oil flows to international markets facing supply constraints. The consecutive weekly drops represent one of the most sustained periods of inventory decline in recent years.

Despite the inventory crunch, oil prices have not surged to the extreme levels some analysts predicted. Multiple factors have kept prices in check, including increased production from other suppliers and demand adjustments in response to higher costs. The supply shock, while significant, has not translated into the catastrophic price spikes that historically accompanied major Middle East disruptions.

The low inventory levels raise concerns about America's ability to respond to future supply disruptions. The Strategic Petroleum Reserve exists specifically to buffer against such shocks, but sustained drawdowns limit that capacity. Energy analysts are watching closely to see whether the administration will take steps to rebuild reserves or whether exports will continue at current pace.

The situation reflects broader tensions in global energy markets. The Iran conflict has removed significant supply from international markets, while robust demand and limited spare capacity from other producers have left little room for error. Gulf Coast refineries continue operating at high capacity to meet both domestic and international demand, but the pace of inventory decline suggests the current trajectory is unsustainable without either reduced exports or increased domestic production.

cards.headline: Trump administration considers taking government stakes in AI companies
cards.teaser: The White House is exploring profit-sharing arrangements with major artificial intelligence firms.
cards.body:
President Trump said his administration will examine whether the U.S. government should take equity stakes in major AI companies, describing the concept as potentially "a beautiful thing." The proposal would allow Americans to benefit from the success of AI companies. Trump plans to meet with artificial intelligence companies soon to discuss the idea further, and talks with OpenAI about a possible government stake are already underway.

The concept has drawn support from across the political spectrum, including interest from Senator Bernie Sanders. The proposal reflects the government's growing recognition of AI's strategic importance, particularly given substantial public investments in the sector through research funding and infrastructure.

cards.headline: Trump pardons former congressman convicted of insider trading
cards.body:
President Donald Trump issued a full pardon for Steve Buyer, a former Indiana Republican congressman who was convicted of insider trading in 2023. The pardon wipes away Buyer's criminal record and any penalties associated with the conviction.

Buyer served in the House of Representatives from 1993 to 2011, representing Indiana's 4th and 5th congressional districts during his tenure. After leaving Congress, he worked as a consultant and lobbyist before his legal troubles began.

In 2023, a federal jury convicted Buyer on charges related to insider trading. Prosecutors alleged he used nonpublic information to make stock trades that generated illegal profits. The conviction came after an investigation into his financial activities following his departure from Congress.

The pardon is the latest in a series of clemency actions by Trump, who has used his presidential pardon power extensively. Trump has previously granted pardons to political allies, former staff members, and others convicted of federal crimes. The pardon power, granted to the president by the Constitution, allows the chief executive to forgive federal crimes and remove associated punishments.

Buyer's pardon adds to ongoing debates about presidential clemency and its use for individuals with political connections to the president. The move drew criticism from ethics watchdogs who argue that pardons for white-collar crimes by former elected officials undermine public trust in government accountability.

cards.headline: Israeli soldier kills seven-month-old baby in West Bank shooting
cards.teaser: An Israeli soldier opened fire on a car in the West Bank, killing a seven-month-old Palestinian infant and wounding the baby's parents.
cards.body:
Israeli troops fired on a vehicle in the West Bank, killing a seven-month-old Palestinian baby and injuring the child's parents, according to Palestinian officials. The infant was later laid to rest in a funeral attended by family members and community mourners.

The Israeli military said a soldier opened fire after troops perceived the vehicle accelerating toward them, viewing it as a potential threat. The baby's grandmother, who was also in the car at the time of the shooting, disputed the military's account of what happened. The military said it is investigating the incident.

cards.teaser: Russia described a Ukrainian drone attack on St Petersburg as unprecedented, prompting the city's governor to urge residents to stay indoors for the first time since the war began.

cards.headline: Israeli strike kills Lebanese general and two soldiers in south Lebanon
cards.teaser: An Israeli military attack on a car in south Lebanon killed three soldiers, including a general, in an incident the Israeli military said it is investigating.
cards.body:
Three Lebanese soldiers, including a general, were killed in an Israeli attack on a vehicle in south Lebanon, where Israeli forces are engaged in fighting with Hezbollah. The strike represents a significant incident involving Lebanese military personnel rather than Hezbollah fighters.

The Israeli military said it is investigating the attack. The deaths occurred in an area where Israeli forces have been conducting operations against Hezbollah, the Iranian-backed militia that operates in southern Lebanon. The incident raises questions about rules of engagement and the risk to Lebanese military forces operating in the conflict zone.

cards.headline: CIA employee accused of funneling millions through fake spy program must remain in detention
cards.teaser: A federal judge ruled that David Rush, a CIA officer found with gold bars, must stay in detention while facing charges of creating a fraudulent program to funnel federal funds to himself.
cards.body:
A federal judge ordered that David Rush, a CIA employee, remain in detention after he was found with gold bars and accused of creating a fake intelligence program. US officials say Rush funneled millions of dollars in federal funds to himself through the fraudulent operation.

The case involves allegations that Rush used his position within the CIA to establish a program that existed only to divert money for his personal benefit. The discovery of gold bars in his possession added to the evidence suggesting financial crimes. The judge's decision to deny bail suggests the court views Rush as either a flight risk or a continuing threat.

cards.headline: Pope Leo begins Spain visit with praise for government's stance on war and migration
cards.teaser: Pope Leo started a seven-day official tour of Spain by commending the country's opposition to war and support for migrants, meeting with refugees and homeless people.
cards.body:
Pope Leo began his seven-day tour of Spain by praising the country's commitment to peace and solidarity, particularly its opposition to war and support for migrants. The pontiff urged political leaders to reject polarization and seek unity rather than dividing populations for political gain.

The Pope made marginalized communities a central focus of his visit, meeting with homeless people in Madrid and migrants in the Canary Islands. This marks his first tour of an EU country outside Italy, reflecting his emphasis on respecting every human being.

cards.headline: Defense Secretary Hegseth invokes immigration as invasion in D-Day anniversary speech
cards.teaser: US Defense Secretary Hegseth used a D-Day anniversary speech in France to describe migration to Europe as an invasion of its beaches, drawing criticism for the rhetoric.
cards.body:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth delivered remarks at a D-Day commemoration in Normandy, marking 82 years since allied forces launched their operation to liberate Nazi-occupied northwestern Europe. During his speech, Hegseth characterized the arrival of migrants on European shores as an "invasion of beaches," urging European nations to counter the migration.

The speech drew immediate criticism for using military language associated with World War II combat to describe immigration during a ceremony honoring those who fought in the war.

cards.headline: FBI fires analysts who worked on memo about Catholic extremist ideology
cards.teaser: FBI Director Kash Patel terminated five analysts connected to a disputed internal memo that addressed concerns about extremism among traditionalist Catholics.
cards.body:
The FBI dismissed several analysts who worked on the Richmond field office memo examining radical traditionalist Catholic ideology. The document, which drew criticism after its release, suggested potential extremist ties within certain Catholic communities.

The firings represent a significant personnel action by Director Patel. The memo had become a point of contention, with critics arguing it unfairly targeted religious groups. The analysts' termination follows sustained scrutiny of the document and the investigative approach it outlined.

cards.headline: Trump pardons former congressman convicted in insider trading case
cards.teaser: President Trump issued a pardon to former Republican Representative Stephen Buyer, who was convicted of insider trading.
cards.body:
The president granted clemency to Buyer, a former GOP congressman who faced criminal charges related to securities fraud. Buyer had been found guilty of using nonpublic information to make stock trades for personal gain.

The pardon removes Buyer's conviction and any associated penalties. The former congressman's case involved allegations that he exploited confidential corporate information to profit in the stock market while serving in Congress.

cards.headline: Witness testifies about victim's injury in Karmelo Anthony murder trial
cards.teaser: A witness at the murder trial of former NBA player Karmelo Anthony described seeing victim Austin Metcalf reveal a severe stab wound.
cards.body:
Testimony continued in the trial of Anthony, who faces charges in the fatal stabbing of Metcalf at a Frisco ISD track meet. A witness told the jury that Metcalf lifted his shirt to show a large wound in the immediate aftermath of the attack.

The trial has included video evidence showing the scene following the stabbing. Witnesses confirmed Metcalf's words and actions in the moments after he was wounded. Anthony had reportedly been asked to leave the opposing team's tent multiple times before the fatal encounter occurred.

cards.headline: Republicans in Congress increasingly willing to oppose Trump agenda
cards.teaser: A growing number of Republican lawmakers have broken ranks with President Trump as midterm election pressures mount.
cards.body:
Vulnerable Republican members of Congress are showing greater willingness to defy the president's legislative priorities. The shift comes as the party faces competitive races in the approaching midterm elections, with some representatives calculating that independence from Trump may benefit their reelection prospects.

The defections represent a change in congressional dynamics, where Republican unity behind the president had previously been strong. Lawmakers are weighing the political risks of opposing Trump against the potential consequences of full alignment in their home districts.

cards.headline: Ukrainian drones strike St. Petersburg in attack Russia calls unprecedented
cards.teaser: Ukraine launched a drone assault on St. Petersburg, prompting Russian officials to urge residents indoors for the first time since the war began.
cards.body:
Ukrainian drones struck St. Petersburg in what Russian authorities called an unprecedented attack on the country's second-largest city. The assault prompted the city's governor to issue an unusual public warning, urging residents to remain indoors—a measure not taken previously during the war.

The strikes represent a significant escalation in Ukrainian drone operations, reaching deeper into Russian territory than before and targeting one of Russia's most important cultural and economic centers. In response, President Putin announced plans to strengthen Russia's air defenses against future Ukrainian drone attacks.

cards.headline: Pope begins Spain visit, praises country's stance on war and migrants
cards.teaser: Pope Leo XIV started a seven-day official tour of Spain, commending the nation's commitment to peace and support for refugees.
cards.body:
The pontiff arrived in Spain for a seven-day official visit, using his opening day to commend the country's international approach. The Pope praised Spain's "active commitment to peace and solidarity among peoples," highlighting its stance on both conflict prevention and migration support.

During the tour, Pope Leo addressed journalists aboard the papal plane, discussing his views on military conflict. He stated that the war in Iran does not qualify as a "just war" according to Catholic teaching.

cards.headline: Multiple states prepare antitrust lawsuit to block Paramount-Warner Bros. merger
cards.teaser: State attorneys general plan legal action against the $110 billion media consolidation deal.
cards.body:
Multiple U.S. states are preparing to file an antitrust lawsuit to prevent the merger between Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery, the $110 billion deal that would create one of the largest entertainment conglomerates in history. The legal challenge adds to mounting regulatory pressure on the combination, which already faces scrutiny from European regulators.

Paramount has offered to sell some of its children's channels to address concerns from European Union antitrust officials. The company has also asked a federal judge to dismiss a separate consumer antitrust lawsuit seeking to block the Warner Bros. Discovery acquisition. The merger would unite two major film studios, streaming platforms, and cable networks under single ownership.

cards.headline: Bitcoin falls below $60,000 to lowest level since October 2024
cards.teaser: The cryptocurrency continues declining despite President Trump's public support for digital assets.
cards.body:
Bitcoin dropped below $60,000, reaching its lowest price point since October 2024 and extending a week of steep losses for cryptocurrency markets. The decline comes despite President Trump's embrace of digital assets and his administration's generally favorable stance toward the crypto industry. The breach of the $60,000 threshold marks a significant psychological barrier for investors.

Bitcoin's recent price crash has wiped out billions in bullish crypto bets as traders who expected continued gains faced mounting losses. The cryptocurrency's struggles have surprised analysts who anticipated political support from the Trump administration would stabilize or boost prices. The selloff reflects broader volatility in risk assets and questions about cryptocurrency's role as an inflation hedge or safe haven investment.

cards.headline: Oil prices remain stable despite historic Middle East supply disruption
cards.teaser: Crude has not reached $200 per barrel even as Iranian conflict creates major supply shock.
cards.body:
Oil prices have remained far below catastrophic levels despite what analysts describe as the biggest supply shock in history stemming from the U.S.-Iran conflict. Crude has not approached $200 per barrel, defying predictions that major Middle East disruptions would send energy costs soaring to unprecedented heights.

Multiple factors have prevented extreme price spikes. These include production increases from other oil-producing nations, demand adjustments as consumers respond to higher prices, and strategic reserve releases. The relative price stability, while oil remains elevated, suggests global markets have more flexibility to absorb supply shocks than in previous decades.

cards.headline: SpaceX IPO draws warnings of retail investor risk
cards.teaser: Financial analysts caution that the highly anticipated public offering may disappoint individual investors.
cards.body:
SpaceX plans to launch what's being called the biggest stock market debut in history on June 12, with an expected valuation of $135 per share. The company will sell 555.6 million shares to raise $75 billion. Up to a quarter of the shares could be reserved for individual investors rather than institutional funds and banks—a notably larger allocation than typical for major IPOs.

Experts have flagged significant downsides for retail investors considering the offering. Investment analysts warn that the IPO could prove costly for individual shareholders, with some predicting it may become one of the most problematic IPOs for this group.

hero.headline: White House AI advisor Sriram Krishnan leaves post
hero.body:
Sriram Krishnan has left his position as White House AI advisor, according to reports. Krishnan is reportedly starting a new institution to continue shaping the Trump administration's AI policy from outside the government.

Krishnan's departure comes as the administration continues to formulate its approach to artificial intelligence regulation and development. His role had involved advising on AI policy matters during a period of rapid technological advancement and growing debate over AI governance.

The new institution Krishnan plans to launch will allow him to maintain influence on AI policy discussions without holding an official government position. This approach mirrors efforts by other former officials who have sought to shape policy from think tanks and advocacy organizations.

Krishnan's exit follows broader discussions within the administration about artificial intelligence strategy. President Donald Trump has publicly discussed deals involving American equity stakes in AI companies, suggesting the administration views AI development as a matter of national economic interest. The coordination between Krishnan's new outside role and existing White House AI initiatives remains to be seen.

The transition reflects the fluid nature of AI policy staffing as the administration works to balance innovation, regulation, and strategic competition in the technology sector. Krishnan's continued involvement through a new institution suggests he will remain a voice in these debates, even without the direct access that comes with a White House position.

cards.headline: Trump administration discusses equity stake in OpenAI
cards.teaser: President Donald Trump said he is discussing deals where the American people could benefit from AI success.
cards.body:
President Donald Trump said the administration is discussing potential deals involving OpenAI that would allow Americans to benefit from AI's success. The discussions suggest the federal government is exploring ways to gain financial returns from the artificial intelligence sector's growth.

Such an arrangement would be unusual, as the government typically does not take equity stakes in private technology companies. OpenAI, creator of ChatGPT, has emerged as a leader in generative AI development and has secured substantial private investment.

cards.headline: Apple prepares Siri revamp and AI updates for WWDC
cards.teaser: Apple's annual developer conference approaches with anticipated changes to its voice assistant and intelligence features.
cards.body:
Apple's Worldwide Developers Conference 2026 is set to showcase a revamp of Siri alongside updates to Apple Intelligence. The conference, which draws developers and media attention each year, will outline the company's software direction.

The Siri updates represent Apple's response to advances in AI assistants from competitors. Apple Intelligence, the company's broader AI initiative, is also expected to receive new features as the company works to integrate artificial intelligence capabilities across its product line.

cards.headline: Scientists revive ancient microbes frozen with Ötzi the Iceman
cards.teaser: Researchers have successfully grown microbes that were frozen with the 5,300-year-old mummy.
cards.body:
Scientists have successfully cultivated ancient microbes that were frozen alongside Ötzi the Iceman for more than 5,000 years. The microorganisms remained viable despite millennia of preservation in ice, raising questions about the boundary between artifacts and living ecosystems.

The discovery has implications for understanding ancient microbial life and preservation. Ötzi, discovered in the Alps in 1991, has provided researchers with insights into Copper Age life, and now the microbes associated with his remains offer another dimension to that research.

cards.headline: Sea star populations see baby boom after massive die-off
cards.teaser: Biologists observe a surprising recovery among sea star populations following widespread mortality events.
cards.body:
Biologists have documented a significant increase in baby sea stars following massive die-offs that devastated populations in recent years. The unexpected baby boom suggests the species may be recovering faster than anticipated.

Sea stars along the Pacific coast experienced widespread mortality due to a wasting disease that caused the animals to lose limbs and disintegrate. The new generation of sea stars offers hope that the populations can rebound from the ecological disruption.

cards.headline: iOS 27 to introduce seven new iPhone features
cards.teaser: Apple's upcoming mobile operating system will bring changes to Find My, animations, and other capabilities.
cards.body:
Apple's iOS 27 will include seven new features for iPhone users when it launches following WWDC. The update includes changes to the Find My feature, new animations, and additional functionality across the operating system.

The release represents Apple's annual refresh of its mobile platform. Details about the features suggest incremental improvements to existing capabilities rather than wholesale redesigns, consistent with Apple's recent approach to iOS updates.

cards.headline: Stellar Blade sequel Blood Rain leaves platform options open
cards.teaser: Developer Shift Up says no platforms are decided for the upcoming game, including Xbox, PC, and PlayStation 5.
cards.body:
Shift Up is keeping platform options open for Stellar Blade: Blood Rain. The developer stated they want to reach as many fans as possible, and has made no final decisions about day-one platforms. Xbox Series, PC, and PlayStation 5 are all potential options for the sequel's launch.

The original Stellar Blade released exclusively on PlayStation 5. This more flexible approach to the sequel's platform strategy represents a potential expansion beyond Sony's console.

hero.headline: Andreeva wins French Open for first Grand Slam title
hero.body:
Russian teenager Mirra Andreeva won the French Open on Saturday, defeating Polish qualifier Maja Chwalinska to claim her first Grand Slam title. The victory marks a breakthrough moment for Andreeva, who emerged from a competitive field to take the championship at Roland Garros.

Chwalinska, ranked 114th in the world, had an unexpected run through the tournament as a qualifier but fell short in the final against the young Russian. Andreeva's path to the title required her to navigate through multiple rounds and overcome the challenge posed by the underdog Pole.

The French Open title represents the pinnacle of clay court tennis and adds Andreeva to the list of Grand Slam champions. At her age, the win positions her as one of the sport's rising stars and signals a potential shift in the competitive landscape of women's tennis.

Grand Slam tournaments are the four most prestigious events in professional tennis, with the French Open being the only one played on clay courts. The surface is known for favoring players with strong baseline games and endurance. Andreeva's victory demonstrates her ability to excel on the demanding red clay of Paris.

The win gives Andreeva significant momentum heading into the grass court season and Wimbledon. For Chwalinska, reaching the final as a qualifier represents a career achievement despite the loss. The Polish player's ranking will see a substantial boost following her performance in Paris.

cards.headline: Browns trade Myles Garrett to Rams
cards.teaser: The Browns have traded defensive end Myles Garrett to the Rams, prompting cornerback Denzel Ward to publicly state his desire to remain in Cleveland.
cards.body:
The Cleveland Browns traded defensive end Myles Garrett to the Los Angeles Rams in a significant defensive roster move. Garrett had been a cornerstone pass rusher for the franchise.

Following the trade, Browns cornerback Denzel Ward expressed his commitment to the team, stating he wants to remain in Cleveland despite the departure of his defensive teammate.

cards.headline: Rays move Steven Matz from rotation to bullpen
cards.teaser: The first-place Rays are shifting left-hander Steven Matz to the bullpen after two poor starts pushed his season ERA to 5.48.
cards.body:
The Tampa Bay Rays have moved left-handed pitcher Steven Matz from the starting rotation to the bullpen. The decision comes after two consecutive poor starts that lifted his earned run average to 5.48 this season.

The first-place Rays are making the change as they look to shore up their rotation while maintaining their division lead.

cards.headline: Wembanyama takes blame for costly turnover in Game 2 loss
cards.teaser: Spurs star Victor Wembanyama admitted urgency led to a late turnover in Friday's Game 2 defeat, vowing to use the frustration as motivation.
cards.body:
San Antonio Spurs star Victor Wembanyama acknowledged that urgency affected his judgment when he turned the ball over late in Friday's Game 2 loss. He expressed frustration with the outcome, saying "This game was ours," but remained focused on moving forward.

Wembanyama plans to use his disappointment as motivation heading into the next matchup. The series is now tied 1-1, with Games 3 and 4 shifting to Vegas.

cards.headline: Twins recall Royce Lewis from Triple-A
cards.teaser: The Twins have brought back infielder Royce Lewis from Triple-A St. Paul, less than three weeks after sending him down to work on mechanics and position flexibility.
cards.body:
The Minnesota Twins recalled infielder Royce Lewis from Triple-A St. Paul after less than three weeks in the minors. The former No. 1 overall draft pick had been optioned to work on his swing mechanics and improve his flexibility across multiple defensive positions.

The quick recall suggests the organization felt Lewis made adequate progress during his brief assignment and is ready to rejoin the major league roster.

cards.headline: Brayden McNabb's status uncertain for Game 3
cards.teaser: Vegas defenseman Brayden McNabb's availability for Game 3 of the Stanley Cup Final remains unclear after he took a puck to the face in Game 2 against Carolina.
cards.body:
Vegas Golden Knights defenseman Brayden McNabb left Game 2 of the Stanley Cup Final after taking a puck to the face. The team has not announced whether he will play in Game 3 against the Carolina Hurricanes.

The series is tied 1-1 as the matchup shifts to Las Vegas for the next two games.

cards.headline: Iran accuses U.S. of denying visas to World Cup staff
cards.teaser: Iran's soccer federation says the United States refused visas for key administrative members of its World Cup team, calling the decision vindictive behavior.
cards.body:
Iran's soccer federation has accused the United States of "vindictive behavior" after technical and administrative staff members were denied visas for the 2026 World Cup. The denials came hours after the U.S. approved visas for Iranian players.

Iran qualified for the tournament, which will be co-hosted by the United States, Canada, and Mexico. The federation characterized the visa refusals for key managerial and administrative personnel as deliberate obstruction.

hero.headline: Taxi Driver Filmmakers and Stars Reunite for 50th Anniversary
hero.teaser: Robert De Niro, Martin Scorsese, Jodie Foster, and Paul Schrader gathered to mark five decades since the iconic film's release.
hero.body:
The creative team and stars behind Taxi Driver gathered at New York's Tribeca film festival to celebrate five decades since the film's release and reflect on its enduring cultural significance. Director Martin Scorsese, actor Robert De Niro, actress Jodie Foster, and screenwriter Paul Schrader participated in a screening at the BMCC Tribeca Performing Arts Center to examine the film's lasting impact.

Released in February 1976, Taxi Driver immediately became a cultural phenomenon. The film earned the Palme d'Or at Cannes and received four Academy Award nominations, including best picture and best actor for De Niro. Foster, who was just 12 when the film was shot, earned a nomination for best supporting actress.

Scorsese emphasized the film's universal appeal despite its age. "It's a sense of being isolated, it's about being lonely and not being able to communicate or connect," he said. "For me, that's universal. It's always going to speak to young people." Schrader noted the film's remarkable staying power. "If we marked the 50th anniversary of a film in 1976, we'd be talking about a 1926 movie," he said. "So it is very peculiar."

De Niro's character, Travis Bickle, is an insomniac cab driver navigating a grimy New York City while struggling with isolation and an inability to connect with others. The script, written by Schrader, meticulously details his descent into violence. "Each page was like a razor blade," Scorsese recalled of reading the screenplay.

De Niro reflected on the film's continued relevance. "Today, I do understand that people are still lonely, especially with the internet, and in light of the pandemic. People are getting more isolated and getting into worlds they shouldn't get into, becoming obsessed with something negative."

The film proved disturbingly prophetic. Though Columbine occurred decades later in 1999, Taxi Driver was shown during the trial of John Hinkley Jr., who attempted to assassinate Ronald Reagan in 1981 while allegedly attempting to impress Foster. The archetype of the alienated young man with violent tendencies has only intensified in modern times, paralleling the rise of extremist internet groups.

Foster discussed the character's complexity. "When I first read the script, there was something absolutely 100% true and authentic about the character's disaffection and loneliness that I didn't really understand at the time," she said. "That's the draw of the antihero."

Scorsese also contrasted the film's gritty 1970s New York setting with today's city. When they filmed in 1975, crime peaked and the city faced financial crisis. "There was something during the shoot where you could feel the temperature and a kind of violence all around you," he said. Schrader lamented the city's transformation. "It was alive," he said of New York in the 1960s and 1970s.

cards.headline: Patrick Godfrey, English Actor Known for Ever After and Stage Work, Dies at 93
cards.teaser: Patrick Godfrey, an English actor who appeared in films, television, and theater for more than five decades, died on Thursday.
cards.body:
Patrick Godfrey, an English actor with a career spanning more than five decades, died on Thursday at age 93. His talent agency, Markham Froggatt Irwin, announced his death on June 5.

Godfrey played Leonardo da Vinci in the 1998 film Ever After: A Cinderella Story, starring Drew Barrymore. Beyond this American film role, he built a substantial career in British television and theater, appearing in productions including Doctor Who, Inspector Morse, and a stage adaptation of Les Misérables.

cards.headline: A24 Horror Film Backrooms Becomes Studio's Highest-Grossing Movie
cards.teaser: The YouTube-inspired horror film crossed $100 million domestically, setting a new record for the independent studio.
cards.body:
A24's Backrooms has become the studio's highest-grossing film at the global box office, surpassing the $100 million mark domestically. The horror film draws from internet folklore depicting endless maze-like spaces that have captured online audiences.

The film's success highlights how content originating from the internet can translate effectively to theatrical releases. Backrooms joins other horror entries like Obsession in demonstrating the commercial viability of adapting web-based material for cinema.

cards.headline: The Cure Performs Rare Tracks at Primavera Sound Festival
cards.teaser: Robert Smith and his band played deep cuts including '2 Late,' 'Wrong Number,' and 'Mint Car' at their first concert since November 2024.
cards.body:
The Cure headlined Spain's Primavera Sound festival with a set that featured rarely performed songs from their extensive catalog. The band played tracks including '2 Late,' 'Wrong Number,' and 'Mint Car,' offering devoted fans material not typically heard in their standard performances.

The concert marked the band's first appearance since November 2024, ending an 18-month absence from live performance. Robert Smith led the group through the set, which balanced the rare selections with their better-known material.

cards.headline: John C. Reilly Says He Urged Leonardo DiCaprio to Skip Titanic for Boogie Nights
cards.teaser: The actor told a podcast he tried convincing DiCaprio to star in Paul Thomas Anderson's film instead of the James Cameron blockbuster.
cards.body:
John C. Reilly recounted his attempt to persuade Leonardo DiCaprio to turn down Titanic in favor of Boogie Nights during an appearance on Ted Danson's podcast Where Everybody Knows Your Name. Reilly said he and director Paul Thomas Anderson were close collaborators and wanted DiCaprio for Anderson's film.

Reilly told DiCaprio that no one would care who was on the boat, attempting to steer him toward the ensemble drama about the adult film industry in the 1970s. DiCaprio ultimately chose Titanic, which became one of the highest-grossing films in history.

cards.headline: Morgan Wallen Cancels Second Pittsburgh Concert Due to Weather Forecast
cards.teaser: The country singer called off a show at Acrisure Stadium with severe weather expected in the area.
cards.body:
Country music artist Morgan Wallen canceled his second scheduled concert at Acrisure Stadium in Pittsburgh due to an incoming severe weather threat. The decision was made to prioritize the safety of concertgoers and staff at the venue.

Wallen had already performed at the stadium earlier in the week, with WWE Hall of Famer Kurt Angle joining him for that show's opening. The cancellation affected fans who had tickets to the follow-up performance.

cards.headline: Peter Phillips Marries Harriet Sperling in Gloucestershire Ceremony
cards.teaser: King Charles' nephew wed the NHS nurse in an intimate ceremony attended by senior British royals including Princess Anne.
cards.body:
Peter Phillips, the son of Princess Anne and nephew of King Charles, married Harriet Sperling in Gloucestershire. Senior members of the British royal family attended the ceremony, which was described as intimate.

Phillips' teenage daughters from a previous marriage participated in the wedding. Sperling works as a nurse for the National Health Service. The ceremony took place in England's Gloucestershire region.

hero.headline: Trump pardons former congressman convicted of insider trading
hero.body:
President Donald Trump issued a full pardon for Steve Buyer, a former Indiana Republican congressman who was convicted of insider trading in 2023. The pardon wipes away Buyer's criminal record and any penalties associated with the conviction.

Buyer served in the House of Representatives from 1993 to 2011, representing Indiana's 4th and 5th congressional districts during his tenure. After leaving Congress, he worked as a consultant and lobbyist before his legal troubles began.

In 2023, a federal jury convicted Buyer on charges related to insider trading. Prosecutors alleged he used nonpublic information to make stock trades that generated illegal profits. The conviction came after an investigation into his financial activities following his departure from Congress.

The pardon is the latest in a series of clemency actions by Trump, who has used his presidential pardon power extensively. Trump has previously granted pardons to political allies, former staff members, and others convicted of federal crimes. The pardon power, granted to the president by the Constitution, allows the chief executive to forgive federal crimes and remove associated punishments.

Buyer's pardon adds to ongoing debates about presidential clemency and its use for individuals with political connections to the president. The move drew criticism from ethics watchdogs who argue that pardons for white-collar crimes by former elected officials undermine public trust in government accountability.

cards.headline: Federal prosecutors launch election fraud probe in California
cards.teaser: The Los Angeles U.S. attorney's office opened an investigation into potential election fraud in California's elections.
cards.body:
The U.S. Justice Department sent a federal prosecutor to observe ballot processing in Los Angeles as California's primary election results continued to be counted. The slow pace of vote tallying prompted unfounded claims of election irregularities from national political figures.

Election experts confirmed that California's deliberate counting process is designed to prevent fraud and ensure accuracy. The system includes multiple verification steps and allows voters to correct errors, which accounts for the extended timeline rather than any problems with election integrity.

cards.headline: Pence opposes pardons for violent Jan. 6 rioters
cards.teaser: Former Vice President Mike Pence said rioters who assaulted police or disrupted the 2020 election certification should not receive pardons.
cards.body:
Former Vice President Mike Pence said Jan. 6 rioters who assaulted police officers, vandalized government property, or sought to disrupt certification of the 2020 presidential election in the 2021 attack on the Capitol should not be pardoned by President Trump. Pence said those individuals should never get a dime.

Pence made the comments during an interview on HBO's Real Time. His remarks address ongoing discussions about presidential pardons for individuals convicted of crimes related to the January 6 Capitol attack. Pence was presiding over the Senate during the 2021 attack and was evacuated from the Capitol as rioters breached the building.

cards.headline: Top Trump AI adviser leaving White House
cards.teaser: Sriram Krishnan, central to the administration's artificial intelligence efforts, is departing his White House position.
cards.body:
Sriram Krishnan, who has been central to the Trump administration's artificial intelligence efforts, is leaving his position at the White House. Krishnan served as a top adviser to the president on AI policy and strategy.

Despite his departure from the White House, Krishnan will probably continue to play an active role in the administration's approach to artificial intelligence technology. The administration has made AI development and regulation a priority as the technology rapidly advances across multiple sectors of the economy.

cards.headline: Hilton, Becerra lead California governor primary
cards.teaser: Republican Steve Hilton and Democrat Xavier Becerra are ahead in early results for California's gubernatorial primary.
cards.body:
Steve Hilton and Xavier Becerra are leading in California's governor primary results. The race features Democrats Katie Porter, Tom Steyer, and Xavier Becerra competing against Republicans Chad Bianco and Steve Hilton for their party nominations. Under California's top-two primary system, the two candidates receiving the most votes, regardless of party, advance to November's general election to replace Governor Gavin Newsom.

The Department of Justice sent a federal prosecutor to Los Angeles on Friday to observe ballot processing as vote counting continues across the state. State officials rejected claims that results were being manipulated, though the extended counting period prompted election-related misinformation.

cards.headline: Deb Haaland wins New Mexico Democratic primary for governor
cards.teaser: Former Biden Interior Secretary Deb Haaland secured the Democratic nomination for New Mexico governor.
cards.body:
Former Biden administration official Deb Haaland won the Democratic primary for New Mexico governor. If elected in November, she would make history as the first female Native American governor in the United States.

Haaland previously served as Interior Secretary before launching her gubernatorial campaign. She represented New Mexico's 1st congressional district in the House of Representatives before joining the Biden Cabinet.

cards.headline: Bill Maher mocks Trump over approval ratings
cards.teaser: The HBO host said he can tell when President Trump is in a bad mood based on whether Trump attacks him on social media.
cards.body:
Comedian Bill Maher joked that he can always tell President Trump's temperament based on whether the president is attacking him on social media. Maher said he knows when the president is in a bad mood because Trump starts tweeting about him.

Maher made the comments during the opening monologue of his HBO late-night show Real Time. The comedian has been a frequent critic of Trump and has sparred with the president on social media throughout Trump's political career.
